releases.notes:
> Scope: **`v1.5.0` → `v1.6.0`** (released together for **NeoForge 1.21.1, Fabric 1.21.1, Forge 1.20.1, NeoForge 26.1.2, and Fabric 26.3**)
> Upgrade notice: **Both server and client must update to `1.6.0` together.** Tested and expected to be compatible with existing saves; backing up important worlds before a major update is always recommended.

---
### New Skill & Gameplay

- **New Skill: Scent Tracking (`X` by default, `Shift + X` to switch modes, 2 Skill Points)**
  - Available in all shifted forms (12s duration, 40s cooldown). Sends out a ground-hugging scent wave that highlights creatures through walls and leaves fading pawprints.
  - **Wild Winds (32 blocks)**: Highlights nearby creatures by disposition — hostile (red), neutral (yellow), friendly (green).
  - **Marked Quarry (64 blocks)**: Look at any visible creature within 24 blocks to mark its scent (no cooldown), then cast to track that species from afar with a bright cyan outline and directional wisps.
  - Range scales with form and weather: `+25%` in Quadruped form, `+20%` under a full moon, and `-25%` in rain.
- **Improved Feral Leap (`Z`)**
  - Improved the feel and targeting of Feral Leap: smoother obstacle clearing and forest landing checks, steadier windup aiming, and a clearer 3D landing indicator with arc preview.
- **Faction Explorer Maps**
  - Werewolf Chieftains sell **Hunter Watchtower** maps, Silver-Oath Moonwardens sell **Werewolf Tribe** maps, and summoned Werewolf Brothers can sell both (14 Emeralds + 1 Compass, up to 2 trades).
- **6 New Advancements & Recipe Unlock**
  - Added six new progression/discovery advancements (including **Howling Werewolf** with the Alpha Badge icon), renamed the first companion advancement to **Werewolves**, and unlocked the **Silver-Oath Crossbow** in the recipe book.

### Visual Effects & Appearance

- **Upgraded Ritual & Active Skill Visuals (`enhanced` / `classic` Styles)**
  - Upgraded the visuals for Moon-Oath rituals, the Alpha Trial ward, Alpha pack summoning, all active skills, transformations, and empty-hand claw slashes. Uses **`enhanced`** style by default.
  - Prefer the classic look? Set `visualStyle = "classic"` under `[effects]` in your client config (`config/howlingwerewolf-client.toml`, or `.json` on Fabric). You can also toggle first-person vignettes and camera feedback independently with `skillScreenEffects`.
- **Glowing Werewolf Eyes**
  - Added a Glowing Eyes toggle in the Skins screen with `*_eye.png` resource-pack support; NPCs and companions automatically dim their eyes while sleeping (configurable for NPCs via `npcGlowingEyes`).

### Companions, Worldgen & Configs

- **Companion Bedtime**
  - Resting werewolf companions seek nearby free beds at night or during thunderstorms (and can pass through wooden doors). Clicking an occupied bed makes your companion yield it right away.
- **Worldgen Polish & Toggles**
  - Hunter Watchtowers now avoid abandoned villages and feature biome variants; naturally spawned and spawn-egg Hunters properly roll Silver-Oath Crossbows.
  - Added server toggles `generateHunterWatchtowers`, `generateWerewolfTribes`, and `spawnVillageHunterPatrols`.
- **Claw Damage Multiplier**
  - Added `gameplay.werewolfClawDamageMultiplier` (default `1.0`, range `0.1–10.0`) to scale empty-hand claw attacks, Bloody Bite, and Feral Leap landings without affecting held weapons or Moonrend % HP damage.
- **Add Other Mods' Foods as Werewolf Meat (`additionalWerewolfMeatEntries`)**
  - Lets players and modpack authors mark foods from other mods as edible werewolf meat (applies only to items with food properties). Supports exact **item IDs**, `*` **wildcards**, and `#` **item tags**.
  - Example (`[gameplay]` in `config/howlingwerewolf-common.toml`, or the matching JSON array in `config/howlingwerewolf-common.json` on Fabric):

```toml
additionalWerewolfMeatEntries = [
    "*meat*",
    "#c:foods/raw_fish",
    "#c:foods/cooked_fish",
    "farmersdelight:ham",
    "*venison*",

releases.notes:
The wilds are no longer empty—Werewolf Tribes have lit their campfires across the wilderness, while Hunter Watchtowers raise silver banners on the edge of villages. **v1.5.0** introduces biome-themed settlements and factions, the **Feral Leap** skill, **Silverhide Armor** and the **Silver-Oath Crossbow**, **Modern Player Overlay** customization, and sweeping guide and balance updates.

## New Settlements & Factions
- **Werewolf Tribes**
  - Generate naturally across **forests, birch forests, taigas, plains, and savannas** using local timber and stone. Each tribe features a central courtyard, the Chieftain's longhouse (complete with an upper-floor Moonbane Pearl altar loft), workshops, storehouse, homes, and a ready-to-use **Moon-Oath ritual site** for starting an Alpha Trial or summoning a werewolf brother.
  - Tribe residents follow full day/night routines, and Hunters cannot spawn within **48 blocks** of tribe buildings.
  - Led by the **Werewolf Chieftain**, who trades and restocks by day and supports the pack with healing potions in combat.
- **Hunter Watchtowers & Silver-Oath Moonwarden**
  - Villages can now generate with a Hunter outpost—watchtower, armory, and training yard (adapted for plains, taiga, desert, and savanna)—alongside persistent patrols of **4–6 Hunters**.
  - Guarded by the **Silver-Oath Moonwarden**, clad in Silverhide armor, supporting patrol allies with Instant Health II potions and offering daytime trades.
- **Faction-Focused Trading & Restocking**
  - Both settlement leaders restock at their work spots during the day (up to twice per game day), with distinct faction specialties and mutually exclusive potions:
    - **Silver-Oath Moonwarden (5 offers)**: Favors silver-ingot and silver-for-pelt trades; potion pool includes **Wolfsbane Potion** only.
    - **Werewolf Chieftain (6 offers)**: Favors Wolfsbane, Wolfsbane-for-pelt, and Moonbane Pearl trades; potion pool includes **Werewolf Potion** only.
    - **Summoned Werewolf Brother (8 offers)**: Unchanged, drawing evenly from all 13 trades.
- **Exploration & Creative Support**
  - Added `/locate structure #howlingwerewolf:werewolf_tribes` and `/locate structure howlingwerewolf:hunter_watchtower`.
  - Added dedicated spawn eggs for the **Werewolf Chieftain**, **Tribe Werewolf**, and **Silver-Oath Moonwarden**.

## New Skill: Feral Leap (Default `Z`)
- Unlocks for **3 Skill Points**. Press `Z` to aim a landing marker, left-click to leap, or right-click to cancel.
- Shares a **15-second cooldown** across all forms and grants **Speed I for 5 seconds** on landing.
- Max horizontal range: **25 blocks** (Werewolf) / **30 blocks** (Quadruped Wolf) / **27 blocks** (Beast).
- Form-specific landing impact:
  - **Werewolf**: 3-block area damage (**base damage 7**, scaled by Claw Damage).
  - **Beast**: 4-block area damage (**base damage 10**, scaled by Claw Damage) plus knockback.
  - **Quadruped Wolf**: Inflicts Slowness on nearby targets.

## New Gear & Weapons
- **Werewolf Pelts & Silverhide Armor**
  - Collect **Werewolf Pelts** from Feral Werewolves, tribe members, or trades, and craft them with Silver Ingots and Wolfsbane into **Silver-Tanned Hide** and a 4-piece armor set.
  - Matches iron armor in protection and durability while being lighter, easier to enchant, and granting a speed boost. Each piece reduces freezing and werewolf damage by **10%**, with an extra **10%** reduction for wearing the full set.
- **Silver-Oath Crossbow**
  - Craftable, compatible with vanilla crossbow enchantments, and also wielded by village patrol Hunters.
  - Arrows deal **25% bonus damage** to werewolves and inflict Weakness I for 2 seconds (once every 5 seconds per target).

## Visual & Model Upgrades
- **Modern Player Overlay**

releases.notes:
- The progression screen (**K** by default) now combines the former Traits and Alpha Trial tabs into a single **Guide** tab. It includes more tutorials and explanations of the mod's gameplay mechanics and crafting recipes.
- Each companion has its own **Ignore My Hits** toggle in the command panel, off by default. When enabled, the companion is protected from damage dealt by its owner, including melee attacks, projectiles, and potions. The setting is saved per companion.
- **Moonblood Surge** now strengthens both the caster and their recruited companions within 16 blocks in the same dimension. It also plays a wolf howl. Hope you enjoy it!
- Adjusted natural damage reduction and the Alpha Werewolf Badge's revival mechanics.
- With the Modern model, the Trial Alpha spawns with one of nine randomly selected coats. The werewolves it summons inherit its coat.
- Adjusted overhead name tags. Wild werewolves and hunters no longer display overhead labels by default.
- Improved the fit of vanilla armor on Modern models.
- Fixed elbow fur flipping outward when the Modern Beast sprints or sneaks on all fours.
- Fixed a rendering crash when some mods replace the vanilla humanoid armor model with their own. Known cases include the Cursium Chestplate from Cataclysm and armor from MCA Reborn. Also fixed transformed players appearing as just a shadow when using MCA Reborn's villager model. With that model, an empty main hand uses the werewolf's first-person rendering again. Werewolf and Beast forms show their claws, while the quadruped wolf form hides the empty hand.
- Added the missing whisker fur on one side of the Modern Beast's muzzle, using the existing textures for all nine coats.
- Redrew the textures for the Moon-Oath Altar, Central Moon-Oath Altar, **Werewolf Potion**, **Wolfsbane Potion**, Silver Sword, Alpha Werewolf Badge, and other items.
- Added the server setting **`preventWerewolfFullMoonSleep`**, off by default. Enable it for a more immersive full moon. Players with werewolf blood cannot use a bed in the Overworld from dusk to dawn during a full moon and will see an action bar message when they try. The rule also applies in human form, so werewolves cannot sleep through the full moon before the forced transformation.
- Added two companion advancements. **Blood-Sworn Brother** is awarded when you recruit your first werewolf companion. **Shadow at Your Side** is awarded when you raise a companion to Tier 3, the highest tier.
- Rebuilt the models and redrew the textures for Hunters and the Silver-Oath Watcher.
- Added compatibility with **Punchy! 3.2b**. After transformation, the werewolf renderer takes over the empty main hand, fixing overlapping human hands and claws in bipedal forms and visible human hands in quadruped wolf form. Human form and a main hand holding an item still use Punchy!'s rendering.
- Added compatibility with **Not Enough Animations**. The Classic werewolf's hidden equipment model now uses the vanilla humanoid rig, preventing player animations from pulling chestplate sleeves and shoulders out of alignment while holding a map or lantern.
- **Added a Minecraft 1.21.1 Fabric branch targeting Java 21, Fabric Loader 0.16.14, and Fabric API 0.116.4+1.21.1. The Minecraft 1.21.11 Fabric branch has been updated to v1.3.8. Maintenance for that branch is paused as of this release.**

releases.notes:
**MAJOR UPDATE — Werewolf brothers join the pack, and Howling Werewolf comes to Fabric!** Summon a wandering werewolf merchant, recruit him as a lasting companion, and send your pack to guard, hunt and even tidy your storage. This release also adds **Minecraft 1.21.11 on Fabric**, and redesigns the werewolf progression screen and the companion UI with a smoother look.

This is the first public release since 1.2.2, so the notes below cover everything added since then.

## 1. Werewolf brothers: merchants and companions
The Moon-Oath altars now answer a second rite. Learn **Pack Oath** on the skill tree, build the altars the same way as for the Alpha Trial, place a **Wolfsbane** on each outer altar and a **Moonbane Pearl** in the centre, then right-click the central altar with an empty hand. A werewolf brother runs in from afar and stays for 10 minutes, at any time of day and any moon phase.
- **Trade:** each merchant brings 6 of 9 trades for Silver Ingots, Wolfsbane, Moonbane Pearls, Werewolf Potions and Wolfsbane Potions. Uses are limited and do not restock.
- **Recruit:** right-click him while holding an **Alpha Werewolf Badge** and confirm. You can keep one companion before the Alpha Trial, and up to three after it, one per Pack Oath rank.
- **Orders:** Follow, Guard, Rest, Sort and Hunt.
  - Only Guard fights: it joins your attacks, protects you and strikes back.
  - Monsters leave a following, resting or sorting companion alone.
- **Sort:** the companion walks around and tidies chests, barrels and, on 1.21.11 and 26.1.2, copper chests, within 16 blocks.
  - Hang a filled item frame on a container to choose what it keeps.
  - Containers it cannot walk up to are sorted from up to 32 blocks away.
- **Hunt:** it leaves for 1.5–3 Minecraft days and brings back meat, hides, ores and more, then rests for two days.
- **Grow:** raise a companion from tier 0 to tier 3 with Moonbane Pearls (2 / 4 / 8). Each tier adds health, damage, damage reduction and regeneration.
- **Care:** recall it from any dimension, revive it with a badge, rename it, change its coat, open its nine-slot pack, or dismiss it (its pack is handed back to you).
- Press **C** for the companion window. The window has a built-in guide, and companions address you as **"my Alpha"** by default; you can change this.

Full guide: [Companions](https://github.com/R-Eatch/howling-werewolf/blob/main/docs/COMPANIONS.md) · [Hunt and trade tables](https://github.com/R-Eatch/howling-werewolf/blob/main/docs/COMPANION-TABLES.md)

## 2. Now on Fabric
Howling Werewolf is now available for **Minecraft 1.21.11 on Fabric**, with the same content as the other editions. It requires **Fabric API**.

## 3. A new progression screen
- The **K** screen has been redrawn as a moonlit canvas. It shows tonight's real moon phase, your form standing before the moon, and your skills along its arcs.
- Use the crescent in the top-right corner to switch between the white **Moonlight** and dark **Nightfall** themes.
- **Long Claws, Tool Claws and Fire Claws** can now be switched off and on again on the Abilities page. Switching costs and refunds nothing.
- The **Equipment: shown / hidden** choice on the skin page is now applied and saved with your skin, and other players see it too.
- If you are not a werewolf yet, the K screen now tells you how to become one.

## 4. Animation, rendering and compatibility
- **Modern Beast:**
  - Its forelimbs now step in pairs.
  - Sprinting turns into a four-legged run, and crouching into a low four-legged prowl.
- **First-person arm fur** now shows on 1.20.1, 1.21.1 and 1.21.11, matching 26.1.2.
- **Sodium and Xenon:** Modern textures no longer shift out of place.
- **Iron's Spells and Better Combat:** when they draw your body in first person, the werewolf model no longer blocks the camera. Third person is unchanged.
- The merchant now uses wolf sounds instead of villager sounds while trading.

## 5. Configuration, commands and new guides

releases.notes:
**MAJOR UPDATE — Meet the new Modern models!** This release brings a fresh look to all three werewolf forms, with **27 new textures**, updated animations, and improved equipment rendering.

## 1. Modern models and textures
The new **Modern** model set covers all three forms: **Werewolf, Quadruped Wolf, and Beast**. Each form comes with **nine texture variants**, bringing the total to **27**, with animations adapted to the new models.
A huge thank-you to **thewolfulti** for creating and sharing these models and textures! The contributed assets are licensed under **CC BY-SA 4.0**, consistent with the mod's existing art license.

## 2. Switching models and configuring NPCs
**Modern is the default for new players.** If you're using an existing save, open the werewolf menu, go to **Skins**, and use the button in the **top-right corner** to switch between **Modern** and **Classic**. Classic is the original model set and remains fully available.
To choose which models werewolf NPCs use, open `config/howlingwerewolf-common.toml` and set the following option under `[gameplay]`:
```toml
npcModelSet = "modern"
```
Use `"modern"` for wild werewolves, the Alpha, and its summoned pack to use the new models and textures, or `"classic"` to keep their original appearance.

## 3. Animation and equipment rendering
This update adapts animations to the new models and fixes several animation and held-item rendering issues. **Elytra also have dedicated rendering support and now display correctly.**
Some equipment may still appear incorrectly on Modern models. If you prefer the original equipment appearance, switch to **Classic** or **disable equipment rendering** in the config.

---

Enjoy the new looks, and have fun!

releases.notes:
Since version 1.0.7, Howling Werewolf has received a major update: three new skins have been added, bringing the total to four switchable in-game skins including the original Adrian coat, along with support for importing custom skins.

* Four built-in skins are now available across Werewolf, Quadruped Wolf, and Beast forms: Adrian, Ashen, Onyx, and Ivory.
* Added an interactive skin preview with form selection, rotation, zoom, mouse tracking, and an equipment visibility toggle.
* Added a Skins menu, paged skin browsing, and a Resource Packs shortcut.
* Added custom skin support through resource packs, including in-game template export, Blockbench painting templates, and English and Chinese creation guides.
* Added multiplayer skin synchronization. Custom skins require the same resource pack on each client; if a skin is missing, Adrian is shown as a temporary fallback without overwriting the saved selection.
* Adjusted the Skill Tree layout by moving Level Reset below the skill list.

Version 1.1.2 has passed in-game testing.

For multiplayer, both the server and clients should be updated to 1.1.2, as the new skin synchronization protocol is not compatible with earlier versions.
